prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but there isn’t a single universal “best” HVAC company for everyone. The right choice depends on your zip code, your budget, the size and age of your home, timeline, brand preferences, and whether you want high-efficiency equipment or financing/warranty options.

If you want, tell me your Atlanta zip code and any priorities (budget, fast install, particular brands, desire for maintenance plan or extended warranty) and I’ll find and compare highly rated local contractors. Meanwhile, here’s a practical way to choose and what to expect.

What to look for in the “best” contractor
- Proper credentials: Georgia HVAC license (and local business license if required), proof of insurance, and NATE-certified technicians if possible.  
- Accurate sizing and design: They should perform a Manual J heat-load calculation (not just “match the old unit”).  
- Clear, written estimate: Breaks down equipment, labor, permit fees, refrigerant, coil/air handler, and any duct work.  
- Equipment options & efficiency: Compare sizes and SEER ratings; higher SEER costs more up front but saves energy.  
- Warranties: Manufacturer parts warranty and a clear labor warranty (ask how long and what’s covered).  
- Permits & code compliance: Contractor should pull local permits and handle inspections.  
- Good reviews and local reputation: Check Google, Yelp, Angi/HomeAdvisor, and BBB for consistent feedback on installs and service.  
- References: Ask for recent local installs you can contact.

Important questions to ask every contractor
- Will you perform a Manual J load calculation?  
- What size and SEER rating do you recommend and why?  
- What brand/model are you proposing and what are the warranties?  
- Is the estimate an all-in price? Who pulls permits?  
- Are technicians NATE-certified? Are you licensed and insured?  
- Do you offer financing or maintenance plans?  
- How long will the install take and what’s your earliest available date?

Ballpark cost (Atlanta, typical central AC replacement)
- Simple condenser replacement only (if coil and air handler ok): roughly $2,000–$5,000.  
- Full system replacement (condenser + coil/air handler, average 2–3.5 ton, mid-efficiency 14–16 SEER): commonly $4,000–$9,000. High-efficiency systems or large homes can be $8k–$15k+. Prices vary with brand, SEER, duct work needs, and access.

Where to find good local contractors quickly
- Ask neighbors/homeowners’ groups and check local Facebook groups or Nextdoor.  
- Use Google Reviews, Yelp, Angi, or HomeAdvisor and read multiple recent reviews (delivery and post-install service matter).  
- Check BBB for complaints and resolution history.

If you want, I can:
- Look up top-rated HVAC companies near your Atlanta zip code and summarize recent reviews, services, and estimated costs; or  
- Draft an email/script you can use to request quotes from 3 contractors.

Which would you prefer? If you want me to find options, please give your zip code and any priorities (budget, brand, timeline).
